title: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
abstract: arXiv:2611.13331v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. While merging Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with Federated Learning (FL) enables rank-based flexibility, the interdependence of the adaptation matrices ($\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$) often complicates optimization. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client level. translated_title: 面向联邦LoRA的随机投影与秩感知学习率
translated_abstract: 在资源受限的分布式客户端上对大规模基础模型进行微调，面临着显著的计算与通信挑战。虽然将低秩适应与联邦学习相结合可以实现基于秩的灵活性，但适应矩阵（A 与 B）之间的相互依赖往往使优化变得复杂。在这项工作中，我们从理论上证明：采用高斯初始化并冻结 A 矩阵的 LoRA 微调，相当于对全量微调的一种随机近似，其中批量梯度会受到随机且与秩相关的扰动。受这一见解的启发，我们提出在客户端层面冻结并周期性地重新采样 A 矩阵。该策略解耦了 A 和 B 的梯度，削弱了 LoRA 的低秩约束，并将计算与上行通信开销降低了 50%，从而允许重新分配……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出在联邦学习中冻结并周期性重采样LoRA的A矩阵，从理论上证明这等价于对全量微调的随机近似，从而解耦A、B梯度并将计算与上行通信开销降低50%。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes freezing and periodically resampling the LoRA A matrix in federated learning, theoretically showing this acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, which decouples the A and B gradients and reduces computational and uplink communication overheads by 50%.
